chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who forgot to enter the state of Ihram until he entered the Haram. He (peace be upon him) said: My father said: He should go out to the Miqat of the people of his land. So if he fears that the Hajj will be missed, he should enter Ihram from his place. So if he is able to go out from the Haram, let him go out, then let him enter Ihram.

key_terms.إحرام: Ihram (ritual state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.ميقات: Miqat (designated boundary stations for entering Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who enters Mecca without entering Ihram?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the specific case of *Nasi'* (forgetfulness) regarding the Miqat, distinguishing it from intentional omission by offering a pragmatic solution to preserve the validity of the Hajj. The scholar highlights the principle of *Rukhsah* (concession), allowing the pilgrim to assume Ihram from within the Haram if time is short, thereby preventing the loss of the entire pilgrimage season. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing strict adherence to ritual boundaries with the practical realities of the pilgrim's circumstances.
